what: paper check v1 on Hiron 2021 (in-sample), 3 runs, prompt v1 (reconstructed byte for byte; sha256 matches the runs)
prompt_v1:
You read a PDF of a design or feasibility study of a power system with PV, batteries or diesel generators. Copy out the numbers listed below exactly as the PDF prints them. Return only JSON, no prose, with exactly two keys: "statements" and "schedule".

statements: one entry for EVERY place where a listed quantity is stated: abstract, text, tables, figure captions and conclusion. If the paper states the same quantity in four places, give four entries, also when the values differ. Never fix, convert, add up, multiply or round a number. Each entry is {"quantity": a name from the list, "value": the number as printed (dot for decimals, no thousands separators), "count": the number of identical units when the paper writes for example 2 x 2.7 MW (then value 2.7 and count 2), else null, "unit": the unit as printed, "condition": "" or a few words when the value belongs to a scenario, height, year or case that makes it a different value, "page": the page in the PDF file counted from 1, "place": one of abstract, text, table, caption, conclusion, "quote": the words around the number copied character for character from the PDF, at least 8 words where the text allows, and it must contain the number}.

Quantity names:
- pv_ac_kw: PV plant AC rating (inverter side), any power unit
- pv_dc_kwp: PV array DC size (kWp, MWp)
- diesel_kw: rated power of the diesel plant or of each diesel unit (use count for 'N x size')
- converter_kw: converter or inverter rating of the battery system
- battery_kw: battery power rating
- peak_load_kw: peak electricity demand
- battery_size: battery capacity in any unit as printed (kWh, MWh, Ah, MAh)
- pv_module_wp: rated power of one PV module (Wp)
- pv_module_count: number of PV modules
- pv_module_area_m2: area of one PV module
- pv_area_m2: land or roof area used by the PV plant
- load_kwh_day: electricity demand per day
- pv_kwh_day: PV energy per day
- diesel_kwh_day: diesel energy per day
- load_kwh_yr: electricity demand per year
- pv_kwh_yr: PV energy per year
- diesel_kwh_yr: diesel energy per year
- energy_served_kwh_yr: total electricity served per year
- ghi_kwh_m2_yr: solar irradiation at the site (per day or per year, unit as printed)
- wind_m_s: wind speed (put the height in condition)
- lcoe_usd_per_kwh: levelised cost of energy or cost of energy of the proposed system (put the scenario in condition)
- base_coe_usd_per_kwh: cost of energy of the system before the project
- npc_usd: net present cost
- capex_usd: total initial capital cost
- annual_cost_usd: total annual cost
- cost_item_usd: one line of a cost breakdown; condition = npc_usd, capex_usd or annual_cost_usd (the total it belongs to)
- om_cost_usd: operation and maintenance cost, any form
- pv_capex_usd_per_kw: PV capital cost per kW or kWp
- diesel_capex_usd_per_kw: diesel generator capital cost per kW
- battery_capex_usd_per_kwh: battery capital cost per kWh
- fuel_price_usd_per_l: diesel fuel price per litre
- discount_rate_frac: discount or interest rate used in the economics
- renewable_fraction_frac: renewable share of the energy served
- battery_rte_frac: battery round trip efficiency
- project_life_yr: project lifetime
- fuel_l_yr: diesel fuel used per year
- co2_kg_yr: CO2 emitted per year

schedule: if the paper prints a table of power flows for one day at a fixed time step (for example hourly), give {"page": page in the PDF file, "label": the table name, "period_h": hours per row, "rows": [one object per printed row: {"time", "load_kw", "pv_to_load_kw", "pv_total_kw", "pv_to_battery_kw", "battery_discharge_kw", "diesel_kw", "curtailed_kw"}]}. Map each printed column to the field it means: pv_to_load_kw is PV power that goes straight to the load, pv_total_kw is all PV output, pv_to_battery_kw is power that charges the battery. Use null for a field the table does not have. Copy every row. If the paper has no such table, schedule is null.
notes: runs 2 and 3: the model wrote numbers as JSON strings, so the strict parser rejected every statement (67 and 69)
run 1: table cells dropped because the PDF text layer prints table headers apart from values (fixed by T12a2)
run 1: the PV column of the hourly table was read as total PV, so P5 (990 kW plant giving 1,990 kW) was not flagged
scoring rule C9 tightened before the v2 runs to P1 on pv_area_m2 only; run 1 then scores 8 of 13
